comparisons.peer_topic: Accrued interest receivable and credit loss policy
comparisons.peer_summary: Accrued interest receivable of $3.7 billion and $2.8 billion at December 31, 2024 and 2023 is excluded from the investment securities portfolio. The Firm does not recognize allowances for credit losses on accrued interest, writing them off no later than 90 days past due, and did not reverse accrued interest for 2024 and 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and JPM disclose accounting policies regarding accrued interest receivable, including exclusion from balance sheet line items and reversal mechanics. C reports excluding $1 billion of accrued interest from consumer loans and reversing it to reduce interest income. JPM reports excluding $3.7 billion from investment securities and explicitly states it did not reverse accrued interest for 2024, contrasting with C's significant reversals.

comparisons.peer_topic: Interest Reversal and Payment Application for Nonaccrual Instruments
comparisons.peer_summary: For nonaccrual instruments, unpaid accrued interest is reversed against Interest income. Payments are applied to principal if collectability is in doubt; otherwise, interest income is recognized on a cash basis, and instruments may return to accrual status if current and collectability is assured.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and MS describe the mechanism of reversing accrued interest against Interest income when receivables are uncollectible or placed on nonaccrual status. C reversed $1.7 billion in 2024, primarily related to credit cards. MS describes the policy that unpaid accrued interest is reversed with an offsetting reduction to Interest income for nonaccrual instruments, but does not disclose a specific reversal amount for 2024.

sentences.text: During the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, the Company reversed accrued interest (primarily related to credit cards) of approximately $1.7 billion and $1.1 billion, respectively.
These reversals of accrued interest are reflected as a reduction to Interest income in the Consolidated Statement of Income.
For any instrument placed on nonaccrual status, the Firm reverses any unpaid interest accrued with an offsetting reduction to Interest income.
